I farm the way we do here, starting from what worked on my land before and only adjusting a little. On my 10.1 mu, wheat and maize go one after the other, so I will use the full 10.1 mu for both crops in their own season. I have well water, so I will not be stingy with irrigation, because once wheat is short of water at jointing or filling, yield drops fast, and maize also needs water around big bell and grain filling. I finished only primary school, but after 50 years I still count carefully: fertilizer costs money, but losing yield costs more, so I will keep fertilizer a little on the safe side, close to what good growers around me do. For wheat I will use an improved variety, enough base fertilizer, then topdress nitrogen once in spring and water with it. For maize I will use hybrid seed, put most fertilizer before or at sowing, then chase some nitrogen at the big flare stage. I will keep rotary tillage because it saves labor for my 2-person household and fits this wheat-maize rotation. I will spray wheat about 2 times and maize about 2 times, depending on weeds, aphids, rust, armyworm, and leaf diseases. If weather is normal, I will aim for steady yield, not gambling on extreme high yield with too much extra cost.
